title: Inert Gas Transfer Cryogenic Cooling Holder Applications and Implications for Electron Microscopy of Battery Interfaces
content: Electron microscopy comprises the premier characterization tool to quantify electrochemical evolution at battery interfaces. The correlative nature of scanning / transmission electron microscope (S/TEM) techniques are well-suited towards providing the morphological, structural, and chemical information required to piece together the puzzle of interfacial losses in batteries. However, preparation of a sample into a compatible form-factor for S/TEM (thinner than 100 nm) that remains representative of real battery interfaces remains an intensive task [1]. Pitfalls in sample preparation can introduce uncertainty and difficulty reproducing results. Chiefly, the reactivity of alkali metal anodes (e.g., Li and Na metal) with air and moisture introduces additional challenges to traditional preparation of samples for proper interfacial imaging. Cryogenic sample preparation of TEM battery samples has become popularized in recent years for the ability to limit reactivity and freeze the solid electrolyte interphase (SEI), preserving the chemistry and structure of the sample throughout the transfer process [1,2]. Cryogenic sample preparation is often challenging to execute and even practiced experts can experience failures when handling small samples under cryogenic environments.
